reforms.description: Canada reformed its Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credit programme to improve cost-effectiveness and targeting of government support for business R&D. Budget 2012 announced simplifications and enhancements to predictability, with all changes fully in effect by 2014. The government made available nearly CAD 1.9 billion over four years (2012–13 to 2015–16) in new direct support for business innovation, exceeding savings from SR&ED programme improvements.
reforms.package_name: SR&ED and Business R&D Support Reform
reforms.component_name: SR&ED simplification and direct grants expansion
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improved targeting and cost-effectiveness of R&D tax credits enhance incentives for private sector innovation and productivity growth; increased direct support for business innovation strengthens allocative efficiency.
reforms.status_evidence: All changes fully in effect by 2014; new direct support made available over 2012–13 to 2015–16.
reforms.importance_rationale: System-wide reform of a major R&D tax credit programme affecting the entire business R&D support landscape, with substantial budget reallocation (CAD 1.9 billion in new direct support).
reforms.source_quote: Budget 2012 announced changes to simplify, enhance predictability and improve the cost-effectiveness of the SR&ED programme (with all changes fully in effect in 2014). Since Budget 2012, the government has made available nearly CAD 1.9 billion over four years (2012-13 to 2015-16) in new direct support for business innovation.

reforms.description: Canada announced the Venture Capital Action Plan (VCAP) in January 2013, a comprehensive strategy deploying CAD 400 million in new government capital over seven to ten years to strengthen the venture capital industry. The plan establishes up to four large-scale funds of funds with private sector investors and interested provinces, structured to attract private capital (targeting CAD 2 in private investment for each CAD 1 in government capital). One fund of funds was established in January 2014 in partnership with Ontario.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Venture capital mobilisation supports scaling of innovative firms and commercialisation of research-based technologies, enhancing productivity and innovation-driven growth.
reforms.status_evidence: One fund of funds established in January 2014 in partnership with Ontario; plan in active deployment.
reforms.importance_rationale: Comprehensive, multi-year strategy with substantial capital deployment (CAD 400 million government + leveraged private capital) establishing a new institutional structure (funds of funds) for venture capital support.
reforms.source_quote: The Government of Canada announced in January 2013 the Venture Capital Action Plan (VCAP), a comprehensive strategy for deploying CAD 400 million in new capital over the next seven to ten years to strengthen Canada's venture capital industry and increase risk financing available to innovative firms.

reforms.description: Canada phased out Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations tax credits to wind down public support to venture capital markets. Ontario completed the phase-out of its Labour-Sponsored Investment Funds tax credit in 2012, and the federal Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations tax credit will be phased out by 2017.
reforms.package_name: Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Tax Credit Phase-Out
reforms.component_name: Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations tax credit elimination
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Phase-out removes an inefficient or distortionary tax instrument, potentially improving allocative efficiency; however, it reduces capital availability for venture investment in the short term, creating a trade-off between instrument efficiency and venture capital supply.
reforms.status_evidence: Ontario completed phase-out in 2012; federal phase-out scheduled by 2017 (in progress as of 2014 survey).
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant policy change affecting venture capital financing instruments, but narrower in scope than comprehensive reform; represents a retrenchment rather than expansion of support.
reforms.source_quote: Ontario completed the phase-out of its Labour-Sponsored Investment Funds tax credit in 2012 and the federal Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations tax credit will be phased out by 2017.

reforms.description: Canada launched the Business Innovation Access Program in March 2014 to connect small and medium-sized enterprises with universities, colleges, and other research institutions to address barriers to commercialisation of ideas, products, and services. The programme provides external business services (planning, marketing) and technical services (specialised testing, product prototyping, process development).
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Facilitates knowledge transfer and commercialisation of research outputs by reducing barriers between SMEs and research institutions, enhancing innovation diffusion and productivity.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant new programme addressing a specific market failure (SME access to research institutions), but narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
reforms.source_quote: In March 2014, the federal government launched the Business Innovation Access Program, to connect small and medium-sized enterprises with universities, colleges and other research institutions to address barriers to the commercialisation of ideas, products and services.

reforms.description: Canada expanded R&D investments in green technologies, including over CAD 1.8 billion in funding for carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies, which has produced four large-scale demonstration projects that are either operational or under construction.
reforms.component_name: Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) Technology Funding
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Mission-oriented R&D in green technologies (CCS) supports long-term productivity growth through technological advancement in a strategically important sector; demonstration projects bridge research and adoption.
reforms.status_evidence: Four large-scale demonstration projects are either operational or under construction, indicating active implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D expansion with substantial budget (CAD 1.8 billion) and tangible outputs (four demonstration projects), but narrower in scope than cross-cutting system reforms.
reforms.source_quote: It has also been expanding tax support to clean energy technologies and increasing R&D investments in "green" technologies. As a share of GDP, Canada's spending on "green" energy R&D (i.e.excluding fossil fuels and nuclear) ranks in the top half of 28 OECD countries. This includes over CAD 1.8 billion in funding for carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies, which to date has produced four large-scale demonstration projects that are either operational or under construction.
